resources.string: What the calculations are based on – and how well it is backed by evidence.
The app gives training guidance, not medical advice. The detailed derivation with bibliography is included with the app’s source code.
The higher your heart rate relative to resting and maximum, the more each minute counts. One hour at your threshold equals 100 points.
With a power meter or estimated power, your ride is compared with your threshold power (FTP). Hard efforts count disproportionately.
Without heart rate or power, your 0–10 rating times ride duration is used. The method has been tested in many sports.
Fitness is your training average over roughly six weeks, fatigue over the last week. Form is the difference; the time spans are a proven convention, not a personal measurement.
The app compares your last week with what you are used to. It flags a jump, not a prediction of injury.
Your weekly average is compared with your own normal range, not a single morning. Single values fluctuate too much.
If your HRV is below your normal range, the app suggests an easy ride instead of a hard one. Studies show similar progress with fewer hard sessions.
Successful endurance athletes ride most sessions easy and only a few hard. At most two hard days per week protect your recovery.

The plan increases work time step by step: first tempo and sweet spot, then threshold, finally short hard intervals such as 4 × 4 minutes. The formats come from studies; the steps in between are practical experience.

The plan increases weekly volume by at most 15 percent and weekly load by at most 30 percent above what you are used to. The well-known 10 percent rule is a rule of thumb; studies rather suggest avoiding big jumps.
About every fourth week you ride roughly 45 percent less, but still regularly and with one short effort. This is established practice, though rarely studied directly in endurance sports.
In the two weeks before your event, volume drops step by step by about half; plans shorter than eight weeks get one week. Intensity and frequency stay, so you arrive fresh but still fit.
